conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for coming in today. I’m Dr. Maya Carter, a perinatal mental-health clinician. My whole job is to support new mothers as they adjust to life after baby, and that includes checking on emotional well-being, not just the baby’s check-ups.

The short questionnaire we’re about to do is called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply ten questions about how you’ve been feeling in the past seven days. It helps us spot things like postpartum depression or anxiety early, when support is easiest to give. Everything you share stays confidential within your medical team, and this is a judgment-free space—no right or wrong answers, only what’s true for you.

Once we finish, we’ll add up the score together and talk about what resources or next steps might feel helpful. Ready to start?

First question: In the past seven days, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? Not much. I used to laugh all the time—little jokes, silly shows—but lately it feels like I’m just too tired or preoccupied. Maybe once or twice I cracked a smile when my husband sent me a meme, but even that felt forced.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I haven’t really… I mean, I can count on one hand the times I’ve even smiled this week. Everything feels heavy, and even when my husband tries to joke, it just bounces off me. I keep thinking, “What’s there to laugh at when I can’t even handle my own baby right?”
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park—but now even the thought of leaving the house feels exhausting. I tell myself I should look forward to things, but it’s like the switch is stuck on “off.” I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a lot. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t nap and I kept thinking it must be something I did—maybe I’m not swaddling right, maybe I ate something that bothered him. When he cries for more than a few minutes I’m sure it’s because I’m failing him somehow. I know in my head that babies cry, but the guilt still crashes over me.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s not breathing right, or I’ll lie awake picturing him rolling off the changing table even though I’m standing right there. Nothing has to trigger it—it just shows up and sits on my chest until I’m exhausted from checking and re-checking.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes… a few times this week it hit me out of nowhere. I’ll be folding laundry and suddenly feel like the walls are closing in, like something awful is about to happen. My heart pounds and I can’t catch my breath. It passes after a few minutes, but in that moment I just want to run out of the house, even though I don’t know what I’m running from.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It’s like the dishes, the laundry, the feedings, the texts I haven’t answered—they all pile up until I feel I’m drowning. Some mornings I sit on the couch with the baby in my arms and think, “How am I going to get through today?” I still do what has to be done, but it feels like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That’s been happening several nights. I finally get him down, but as soon as my head hits the pillow my mind starts racing—what if he wakes up screaming, what if I’m too tired tomorrow to keep him safe, what if I’m just failing him? I’ll lie there for an hour or two, sometimes drift off around two or three, then jerk awake at every little sound. I’m exhausted, but sleep feels impossible.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the week, really. It’s like a gray cloud parked over me. I’ll be holding the baby and tears just start leaking out. I look at other moms on social media smiling and going to coffee dates, and I feel like I’m the only one who can’t get it together. I keep telling myself I should be grateful—he’s healthy, I’m physically okay—but the sadness is just there, heavy in my chest.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried three, maybe four times since last week. Once was when he wouldn’t latch and I felt like my body was failing him; another time I dropped a bottle and the formula spilled everywhere and I just sat on the floor sobbing. It feels like the tears are right under the surface all the time lately.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel overwhelmed and sad, but I’ve never wanted to hurt myself. I just want to feel like me again—like a good mom—without this constant weight.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note

Patient: Postpartum mother, 1 week post-delivery

Symptoms endorsed:
- Marked anhedonia (minimal laughter, loss of anticipatory enjoyment)
- Pervasive low mood, tearfulness most days
- Excessive guilt/self-blame regarding infant care
- Clinically significant insomnia when infant sleeps
- Recurrent, unprovoked anxiety (racing heart, worry about infant safety)
- Discrete panic episodes (dyspnea, chest pressure, urge to flee)
- Feeling overwhelmed/drowning in daily tasks

Pattern: Consistent with moderate-to-severe postpartum mood/anxiety distress; no current self-harm ideation (denied on Q10).

Risk factors identified:
- Persistent sadness, crying spells
- Loss of pleasure in previously enjoyed activities
- Sleep disruption not solely attributable to infant care
- Heightened anxiety/panic symptoms
- Strong maternal guilt/inadequacy cognitions

Screening impression: High clinical concern for postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; safety risk presently low (no self-harm thoughts). Recommend expedited formal evaluation and follow-up monitoring.
